children.title: Title
children.body: These rules are the Cadastral Survey Rules 2021.

children.title: Purpose of these rules
children.body: The purpose of these rules is to specify standards for the conduct of cadastral surveys and cadastral survey datasets.

children.transBody: 이 규칙의 목적은 지적측량과 지적측량 성과묶음(CSD)의 수행 기준을 정하는 데 있다.

children.title: Duty of surveyor when defining boundary by survey
children.body:
When defining a boundary by survey, a cadastral surveyor must—
gather all evidence relevant to the definition of the boundary and its boundary points; and
interpret that evidence in accordance with all relevant enactments and rules of law; and
use that evidence to determine the correct position of the boundary and boundary points in relation to other boundaries and boundary points.

children.title: Right-line boundaries
children.body: A right-line boundary must follow the shortest distance between 2 boundary points.

children.transBody: 직선 경계는 두 경계점을 잇는 최단거리를 따른다.

children.title: Arc boundaries
children.body: An arc boundary must follow part of the circumference of a horizontal circle.

children.title: Irregular boundaries
children.body:
(1) An irregular boundary must follow an irregular line.
(2) An irregular boundary must not be used unless expressly allowed by these rules.
(3) An existing irregular boundary on a new primary parcel must be converted to 1 or more right-line boundaries unless it is—
accepted in accordance with rule 15 ; or
part of a new primary parcel that is—
over 20 ha and comprises more than 80% of the existing primary parcel being extinguished; or
over 100 ha; or
a former water boundary.

children.title: Water boundaries
children.body:
(1) A water boundary must follow the landward margin of—
a river bed or a stream bed; or
a lake bed; or
a tidal area.
(2) If the margin of a water body has moved as a result of accretion or erosion,—
any erosion that affects the water boundary must be accounted for unless the boundary is accepted under rule 15 ; and
subject to paragraph (a), the boundary may be adopted in its previously defined position if entitlement to accretion is not being claimed.
(3) If the margin of a water body has moved by processes other than accretion or erosion, the existing water boundary may be—
adopted and set in its previously defined position as an irregular boundary; or
converted to 1 or more right-line boundaries.

children.title: Water centre-line boundaries
children.body:
(1) A water centre-line boundary follows the line midway between the landward margins of a stream or river bed.
(2) An existing irregular boundary that followed the centre-line of a water body may be adopted in its previously defined position as a water centre-line boundary.
(3) A new boundary must not be a water centre-line boundary.

children.title: Height-limited boundaries
children.body:
(1) A height-limited boundary must define the upper or lower extent of a parcel.
(2) The boundary must be—
a surface that is mathematically described, if at least 1 point has a reduced level; or
a surface of a water body or the bed of a water body.

children.title: Acceptance of boundary
children.body:
(1) In these rules, a boundary is accepted if the boundary is adopted without having to comply with an accuracy standard.
(2) An existing primary parcel boundary and its associated boundary points may be accepted if—
there is no risk of the boundary encroaching on another parcel; and
the boundary is part of a new primary parcel over 20 ha that comprises more than 80% of the existing primary parcel being extinguished; and
any 1 of the following applies:
the boundary is a right-line boundary that does not have a boundary bearing or a boundary distance in an approved CSD; or
the boundary has a magnetic bearing and the reorientation of the bearing cannot be determined without measurement; or
the boundary is part of the balance of a title that is to remain limited as to parcels or remain a Hawke’s Bay interim title and its boundary points do not meet the class C boundary accuracy stated in item (iii) of table 2 in rule 27(1) ; or
the boundary is an existing water boundary or water centre-line boundary that is part of the balance of a title that is to remain limited as to parcels or remain a Hawke’s Bay interim title; or
the boundary is an existing irregular boundary.
(3) An existing boundary and boundary points of a balance parcel or residue parcel that is not common with another new parcel on the survey may be accepted.
(4) An existing boundary and its associated boundary points that are part of a new primary parcel over 100 ha and that are not in common with another new parcel on the survey that is 100 ha or less may be accepted.

children.title: Horizontal datum: orientation
children.body:
(1) Every bearing in a cadastral survey that defines or marks a new primary parcel boundary point must be oriented in terms of an official projection applicable to the area ( see Schedule 3 ).
(2) However, subclause (1) does not apply if the survey does not make a new field measurement.
(3) Every bearing in a cadastral survey must be expressed in terms of the same horizontal projection.

(2) 다만, 현지에서 새로 관측하지 아니하는 측량에는 제1항을 적용하지 아니한다.
(3) 지적측량의 모든 방위는 같은 수평 투영법을 기준으로 나타내어야 한다.

children.title: Horizontal datum: connection
children.body:
(1) A new boundary point, a new boundary mark, and an old boundary mark on a primary parcel being created must be connected by 1 or more vectors to—
a cadastral survey network mark ( see Schedule 4 ) within 1,000 m, where one exists; or
any cadastral survey network mark, where one does not exist within 1,000 m.
(2) The vectors required by subclause (1) must be adopted or measured.

children.title: Vertical datum
children.body:
(1) All reduced levels in a survey must be expressed in terms of a single official vertical datum ( see Schedule 5 ).
(2) If 1 or more vertical control marks ( see Schedule 6 ) exist within 1,000 m of any new height-limited boundary point that is defined by a reduced level, at least 1 of those vertical control marks must be included in the survey.
(3) If no vertical control mark exists within 1,000 m of any boundary point referred to in subclause (2), a vertical control mark at any distance must be included in the survey.

children.title: Accuracy of non-boundary marks
children.body:
(1) The horizontal accuracy between any 2 new or old non-boundary marks must not exceed—
0.025 + (dist × 0.00005) m to a maximum of 0.20 m
where dist is the horizontal distance between the marks in metres.
(2) The vertical accuracy between any 2 new or old non-boundary marks must not exceed—
0.030 + (dist × 0.0001) m to a maximum of 0.20 m
where dist is the slope distance between the marks in metres.

children.title: Accuracy of water, water centre-line, and irregular boundaries
children.body:
(1) Accuracy classes do not apply to a water boundary, a water centre-line boundary, or an irregular boundary.
(2) The position of a water boundary, a water centre-line boundary, or an irregular boundary, including an adopted boundary, must be determined to a sufficient level of accuracy to take into account—
the risk of overlap or ambiguity in boundaries, including a water boundary on the other side of the water body; and
any statutory requirement applying to the width or size of the related water bodies; and
the potential for the margin of the water body to move and for the water-related boundary to move or become permanent as a result of that movement; and
the nature of the physical feature that defines the water body margin; and
the value of the land and the intensity of the land use.
(3) However, subclause (2) does not apply to accepted water boundaries, accepted water centre-line boundaries, or accepted irregular boundaries.

children.title: Boundaries must be marked
children.body:
(1) A new boundary point on a new primary parcel must be marked, if practicable, unless—
it is a boundary point that is only between new parcels that are all intended to remain in the same Crown or territorial authority ownership; or
the Māori Land Court does not require the boundary to be marked; or
it is a boundary point that is only between parcels that are required to be, or as a result of the survey will be required to be, held in common ownership; or
it is on a boundary where the parcels on each side of that boundary are required to be, or as a result of the survey will be required to be, subject to reciprocal rights of way; or
it is unlikely that it will need to be physically located in the foreseeable future because of the terrain, ground cover, or protected vegetation; or
it is a boundary point that results from an existing irregular boundary, water boundary, or water centre-line boundary that is being converted to a class B right-line boundary; or
it coincides with a water boundary or a water centre-line boundary.
(2) The following boundary points on an existing boundary of a new primary parcel must be marked, if practicable:
a boundary point that is subject to conflict:
an existing boundary whose definition in an approved CSD is insufficient to enable its compliance with the applicable accuracy standard to be determined:
an existing boundary that is only defined on a diagram on transfer:
an existing boundary of a parcel whose limitation as to parcels is being uplifted:
an existing boundary of a parcel to support an application to make a Hawke’s Bay interim title conclusive:
an existing boundary of a parcel that is subject to a claim for adverse possession:
an existing boundary or boundary point that was created on a Māori land CSD that is annotated “computed plan – areas and boundaries not defined by survey” :
a boundary point that was previously an unmarked non-primary parcel boundary point.
(3) A boundary of a parcel that is to remain limited as to parcels must not be marked unless it is also part of a parcel that is required by subclause (2)﻿(d) to be marked.

children.title: Accounting for primary parcels
children.body:
(1) This rule applies if a CSD creates a new primary parcel.
(2) All land in existing primary parcels being extinguished must be included in 1 or more new primary parcels, residue parcels, or balance parcels.
(3) If the new primary parcel has a height-limited boundary, all space occupied by existing primary parcels being extinguished must be included in 1 or more new primary parcels, residue parcels, or balance parcels.

children.title: Parcel areas
children.body:
(1) An area must be assigned to a primary parcel unless it is a residue parcel or balance parcel, and the area must include the areas of all movable marginal strips in that primary parcel.
(2) An area must be assigned to a parcel intended for a lease unless the parcel is defined by 1 or more permanent structure boundaries.
(3) An area must be assigned to a portion of land being claimed as accretion, dry stream bed, or adverse possession.
(4) If a parcel requires an area under this rule and its shape varies with height, the required area is the area of the polygon described by the extent of the parcel when vertically projected onto the horizontal plane.
(5) An area assigned to a parcel—
must be correctly calculated from its boundary information; and
must be expressed in hectares; and
must not be less than 0.0001 ha; and
may be rounded to 1 part in 1,000 or 0.0001 ha, whichever is greater.

children.title: Classes A and B with inaccurate relationship to underlying parcel
children.body:
(1) If the underlying parcel is not being created by the survey, the relationship of a non-primary parcel boundary to the underlying primary parcel—
may be inaccurately determined if class B accuracies would normally apply:
must be inaccurately determined if none of the underlying parcel boundaries meet the applicable accuracy standard.
(2) If subclause (1) or rule 110(3) has been applied,—
the intersecting non-primary boundaries must be class D and the coincident non-primary boundaries must be accepted; and
bearings must be oriented in terms of an official projection applicable to the area; and
the survey must be connected to a minimum of 2 nearby cadastral survey network marks; and
the cadastral survey network marks may be adopted; and
every class A non-primary parcel boundary point must be within 150 m of a PRM; and
every class B non-primary parcel boundary point must be within 500 m of a PRM; and
the survey must include at least 3 PRMs, each within the applicable distance of a boundary point in paragraph (e) or (f); and
every boundary point that is not class D must be connected by 1 or more vectors to at least 1 PRM.
(3) If the underlying parcel is not being created by the survey and the relationship of a non-primary parcel to the underlying parcel is being accurately determined, a non-primary boundary that intersects an underlying parcel boundary may be class D and the coincident boundaries may be accepted.
(4) If the underlying parcel is being created by the survey and the non-primary parcel intersects or coincides with an accepted boundary, the intersection must be class D and the coincident boundaries must be accepted.
(5) Class D boundaries on an existing non-primary parcel must be upgraded to class A if the underlying primary parcel is being created with class A boundaries.
(6) This rule does not apply if the non-primary parcel is for a unit or a lease.

children.title: Class C for non-primary parcels
children.body:
(1) Class C accuracies may be used for boundaries and associated boundary points of a non-primary parcel where that boundary intersects or coincides with a boundary of a new primary parcel that is—
over 20 ha and comprises more than 80% of the existing primary parcel being extinguished; or
over 100 ha.
(2) Class C accuracies may be used for the boundaries and associated boundary points of a parcel that is for a covenant that would otherwise require class B accuracies.
(3) Class C accuracies may be used for boundaries and associated boundary points of a new non-primary parcel for an easement if the underlying parcel or parcels are—
not being created by the survey; and
held in a single estate record with an area greater than 100 ha.

children.title: Permanent structure boundary
children.body:
(1) A permanent structure boundary may be used only for a parcel that is intended for—
a right under the Unit Titles Act 2010 , if at least part of the permanent structure is on the same underlying parcel or parcels as the unit development, but may encroach onto an adjoining parcel; or
a lease where the lease boundary is located in relation to the permanent structure, if at least part of the permanent structure is on the same underlying parcel as that lease, but may encroach onto an adjoining parcel; or
a right over or appurtenant to a base right described in paragraph (a) or (b), if the right will expire before or at the same time as the base right, and at least part of the permanent structure is on the same underlying parcel as the base right; or
an easement or a covenant whose use is directly related to the permanent structure and the right is expected to become redundant if that permanent structure ceases to exist.
(2) A permanent structure boundary must—
follow a described part of a permanent structure; or
be unambiguously defined in relation to points on the interior or exterior of a permanent structure.

children.body:

no changes are being made to the parcel boundaries; and

(3) If subclause (2) has been applied, the existing parcel appellation must be retained.
(4) The boundary of a new parcel may be accepted if it is common with an unchanged parcel that is not a future development unit.

children.title: Referencing height-limited boundary points
children.body:
(1) A new height-limited boundary point on a unit parcel must be referenced to a PRM.
(2) A new height-limited boundary point on a parcel for an easement, a lease, or a covenant does not require a PRM.
(3) A new height-limited boundary point that coincides with an accepted boundary does not require a PRM.
(4) If a boundary point is required to be referenced, that boundary point must—
be within 150 m of a PRM if it is class A:
be within 500 m of a PRM if it is class B.
(5) The survey must include a minimum of 2 PRMs with reduced levels that are each within the applicable distance in subclause (4) of at least 1 boundary point that is required to be referenced.

(2) 지역권·임차·약정을 위한 필지의 새 높이 한정 경계점에는 영구 참조표지가 필요하지 아니하다.

(4) 참조측량을 하여야 하는 경계점은 다음 거리 안에 영구 참조표지가 있어야 한다.
A급이면 150m 안
B급이면 500m 안
(5) 측량에는 참조측량 대상 경계점 가운데 적어도 하나로부터 제4항의 해당 거리 안에 있는, 표고 성과를 가진 영구 참조표지를 적어도 2개 포함하여야 한다.

children.title: Height-limited boundary points on existing unit developments
children.body:
(1) The reduced levels in a unit title development must be expressed in terms of the previously deposited CSD for the unit title development.
(2) If an unofficial datum is used, a vertical control mark in accordance with rule 18(2) and (3) must be provided with a reduced level in terms of the unit title development.

children.title: Reference marks where non-primary parcel marked

children.title: Accepting existing water boundaries
children.body: If a new non-primary water boundary coincides with an existing primary parcel water boundary, it may be accepted irrespective of its accuracy or its relationship to the current physical position of the water boundary.

children.title: Offsetting MHWS or MLWS
children.body: A new non-primary parcel water boundary at MHWS or MLWS may be offset from an accepted water boundary without determining the true relationship between the 2 boundaries.

children.title: Class and dimensions of intersecting boundaries
children.body:
(1) If a right-line boundary intersects an accepted water boundary,—
the bearing must be defined to class A, class B, or class C accuracies (as appropriate); and
the distance must match the accuracy of the water boundary as determined under rule 29(2) and must be class D.
(2) If a right-line boundary intersects an offset water boundary ( see rule 68 ),—
the bearing must be defined to class A, class B, or class C accuracies (as appropriate); but
no distance is required for that boundary.

children.title: Content of CSD
children.body:
A CSD must include—
a record of survey as specified in subpart 2 ; and
a title plan as specified in subpart 4 whenever a new parcel is created; and
a dataset description, including—
parcel appellations for all new primary parcels; and
the survey purpose for land transfer CSDs; and
the appellation of the land under survey for land transfer CSDs; and
a survey report in accordance with rule 72 ; and
all relevant field information, in a form that ensures permanent usability; and
an accurate record of the position of any new water boundary.

children.title: Information to be included in survey report
children.body:
A survey report must contain the following information:
the purpose for which the survey was conducted, including reference to the statutory provisions relevant to achieving that purpose where it is not otherwise clear:
an explanation of why a CSD for a Crown subdivision does not include a certificate under section 223 of the Resource Management Act 1991 :
the basis for determining the orientation of bearings:
the basis for any bearing adjustment applied to an adopted bearing:
the basis for determining the origin of levels:
details of any conflict and how it was resolved:
reasons for not relying on an old survey mark:
information about old survey marks searched for and not found, or destroyed, if the information cannot be recorded in the record of survey in accordance with rule 80(7):
reasons for, and details of, decisions made about an existing boundary defined by survey, and the information considered in reaching those decisions:
if a movable marginal strip is included in a CSD, a description of the method used to determine its existence:
information about the accuracy of the determination of any water boundary, water centre-line boundary, or irregular boundary, and the factors taken into account, as specified in rule 29(2) :
any information as to why the physical margin of the water body is no longer coincident with an adopted water boundary for the purpose of rule 10 :
reasons why it was impracticable to mark any boundary point in terms of rule 35 :
details to support an exemption from marking a boundary point under the provisions in rule 35(1)﻿(a) to (e) :
a description of the type of equipment and methods used to ensure compliance with the accuracy standards in these rules:
reference to any prior correspondence with LINZ about issues relevant to the application of these rules to the CSD:
notification from the Māori Land Court of a non-standard appellation used under rule 44 :
notification from the Māori Land Court to support a boundary marking exemption under rule 35(1)﻿(b) .

children.title: Units of measure for CSDs
children.body:
(1) A distance and a reduced level must be expressed in metres.
(2) A bearing must be expressed in sexagesimal degrees, minutes, and seconds notation, clockwise from north.
(3) A bearing, a distance, a reduced level, and an area must be recorded to sufficient significant figures to reflect the accuracy requirements in these rules.
(4) A horizontal distance and area must be reduced to the ellipsoid used for the official geodetic datum as defined in Schedule 3 .

children.body:

a survey diagram as defined in subpart 3; and
a list of CSDs used and, if a CSD number is not unique, the land district of the CSD; and

children.title: Survey mark information
children.body:
(1) A record of survey must include all survey marks and points used for the purposes of the cadastral survey, but does not have to include accepted boundary points.
(2) New survey marks and points, and renewed, reinstated, or disturbed survey marks, must be given a unique name that consists of the following components in the following order:
an abbreviation that describes the physical mark type, or “UNMK” if there is no mark:
a unique alpha-numeric identifier:
the CSD number.
(3) An existing survey mark with a name that is not unique may be made unique within the CSD by adding a unique numeric identifier within round brackets before the CSD number.
(4) An undisturbed old mark, removed mark, adopted mark, or point with a unique name must retain that name.
(5) A record of survey must indicate whether a survey mark is disturbed, renewed, or removed.
(6) A record of survey must identify a boundary point that is impracticable to mark in terms of rule 35 .
(7) A record of survey must identify whether a survey mark is searched for and not found, or destroyed, but, if that information cannot be recorded in the record of survey, it must be included in the survey report in accordance with rule 72(h) .
(8) For any PRM, the record of survey must describe the relationship to ground level and its situation, for example, on a berm, carriageway, kerb, or footpath.

children.title: Information about occupation and physical features
children.body:
(1) In this rule, occupation means the physical features that describe the extent of an occupier’s use of land.
(2) A record of survey must include the following occupation information in graphic form:
the nature of the physical feature; and
the age of the physical feature; and
the relationship, by vector, distance, or description, between the occupation and the boundary or boundary position.
(3) Occupation information must be provided in relation to—
each new primary parcel boundary point; and
each existing boundary point that is being marked, or is required by rule 35(2) or 109(1) to be marked, and each related boundary line.
(4) If subclause (3) applies and there is no occupation, a “No Occupation” annotation must be recorded against that boundary point and related boundary lines.

lease; or
easement in a cross lease development; or
interest that is not defined in an approved CSD.

children.title: Parcel boundaries subject to ground movement
Re-establishing boundaries affected by ground movement
children.body:
(1) All affected primary parcel boundaries must be defined by survey and marked, if practicable, unless they can be accepted under rule 15 .
(2) A boundary affected by fault zone movement must reflect that distortion and may include the creation of new boundary angles.
(3) Boundaries being defined by survey in greater Christchurch must take into account Canterbury earthquake movement.
(4) If an affected water boundary is to be retained in its former position under rule 10(2) or (3) , the boundary must be accepted.
(5) If an affected water centre-line boundary is to be retained in its former position under rule 11(2) , the boundary must be accepted.

children.title: Defining non-primary parcel boundaries
children.body:
(1) This rule applies if the underlying parcel is not being created by the survey.
(2) An underlying parcel boundary affected by Canterbury earthquake movement with class A or class B boundaries must be defined by survey and marked, if practicable, if a new non-primary parcel boundary coincides with or intersects it.
(3) If the underlying parcel boundaries are affected by movement other than Canterbury earthquake movement, the non-primary parcel boundaries may be inaccurately determined and the requirements in rule 51(2) apply.
(4) For a new unit title or cross lease development, a new underlying parcel must be created before a new record of title is issued if—
any underlying parcel boundaries are affected; or
redefinition of an affected boundary on the underlying parcel has not already been recorded in the relevant tenure system.
(5) For an existing unit title development where a record of title for an existing unit is being retained, an underlying affected boundary that is not coincident with or intersected by a new non-primary parcel boundary may be accepted.

children.title: Redefinition of underlying parcel boundaries in greater Christchurch
children.body:
(1) A CSD that includes a new non-primary parcel, but not a new underlying parcel, may record the redefinition of a coincident or intersected underlying parcel boundary only if—
the underlying parcel boundary has moved due to Canterbury earthquake movement; and
the redefinition of all of the boundaries of the underlying parcel is not being recorded in that tenure system.
(2) If a CSD records a redefinition of an underlying parcel boundary under subclause (1), the title diagram must—
depict the appellation of the underlying parcel; and
depict all redefined underlying boundaries; and
depict the relationship between a redefined boundary and other underlying parcel boundaries; and
annotate a redefined boundary with “Redefined boundary of [ underlying parcel appellation ]” ; and
include, at the end of the dataset description, the words “and partial redefinition of [ underlying parcel appellation ]” .

children.body: (1) A boundary reinstatement survey must not be used if the boundary point being reinstated is— on an existing water boundary, water centre-line boundary, or irregular boundary; or on a boundary of land held in a record of title that is limited as to parcels; or on a Māori land CSD that is annotated “computed plan – areas and boundaries not defined by survey” . (3) A complex boundary reinstatement survey must comply with rules 16 and 18 to 37 and its CSD must comply with rules 71 to 91 . (4) All other boundary reinstatement surveys may be recorded on a simple boundary reinstatement CSD as specified in subparts 4 and 5 . children.origBody: The Rules for Cadastral Survey 2010 (SR 2010/492) are revoked.
children.transBody: 「지적측량규칙 2010」(SR 2010/492)은 폐지한다.

children.title: Existing surveys may be completed under Rules for Cadastral Survey 2010
children.body: A survey started before the date of commencement of these rules may be completed under the Rules for Cadastral Survey 2010 , as long as the CSD is lodged before 25 February 2022.
children.origTitle: Existing surveys may be completed under Rules for Cadastral Survey 2010

children.title: accepted

children.origBody: accepted has the meaning given to it by rule 15

children.title: Act
children.body: Act means the Cadastral Survey Act 2002
children.origBody: Act means the Cadastral Survey Act 2002
children.transBody: "법"이란 「지적측량법 2002」를 말한다.

children.title: adopt

children.origBody: adopt has the meaning given to it by rule 14

children.title: affected boundary
children.body: affected boundary has the meaning given to it by rule 108
children.origBody: affected boundary has the meaning given to it by rule 108
children.transBody: "영향받은 경계"란 제108조에서 정하는 뜻을 말한다.

children.title: approved CSD
children.body:
approved CSD —
(a) means a CSD determined by the chief executive under section 9 of the Act to comply with these rules; and
(b) includes a CSD approved under former Acts and regulations; but
(c) does not include a CSD lodged only for recording purposes

children.transBody:
"승인된 성과묶음"이란 다음을 말한다.
(a) 법 제9조에 따라 청장이 이 규칙에 맞는다고 판정한 성과묶음을 말한다.
(b) 옛 법률과 규칙에 따라 승인된 성과묶음을 포함한다.
(c) 다만, 기재만을 위하여 제출된 성과묶음은 포함하지 아니한다.

children.title: balance parcel
children.body:
balance parcel means the portion of 1 of the following primary parcels that is intended to remain after a part has been removed by survey:
(a) a railway parcel that is not in a record of title:
(b) a road parcel:
(c) a fixed marginal strip parcel:
(d) the bed of a lake, river, stream, or the sea:
(e) an access way or service lane that is not in a record of title

children.transBody:

children.title: boundary point

children.title: cadastral survey dataset

children.title: cadastre
children.body: cadastre has the same meaning as in section 4 of the Act
children.origBody: cadastre has the same meaning as in section 4 of the Act
children.transBody: "지적(地籍)"이란 법 제4조에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: Canterbury earthquake movement
children.body: Canterbury earthquake movement has the meaning given to it by rule 108
children.origBody: Canterbury earthquake movement has the meaning given to it by rule 108
children.transBody: "캔터베리 지진 변동"이란 제108조에서 정하는 뜻을 말한다.

children.title: centre-line easement
children.body: centre-line easement means an easement that is spatially represented by 1 or more lines along its centre
children.origBody: centre-line easement means an easement that is spatially represented by 1 or more lines along its centre
children.transBody: "중심선 지역권"이란 그 중심을 따르는 하나 이상의 선으로 공간을 나타내는 지역권을 말한다.

children.title: chief executive
children.body: chief executive has the same meaning as in section 4 of the Act
children.origBody: chief executive has the same meaning as in section 4 of the Act
children.transBody: "청장"이란 법 제4조에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: common marine and coastal area
children.body: common marine and coastal area has the same meaning as in section 9(1) of the Marine and Coastal Area (Takutai Moana) Act 2011
children.origBody: common marine and coastal area has the same meaning as in section 9(1) of the Marine and Coastal Area (Takutai Moana) Act 2011
children.transBody: "공유 해면·연안구역"이란 「해양·연안구역(타쿠타이 모아나)법 2011」 제9조제1항에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: company lease
children.body: company lease has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Resource Management Act 1991
children.origBody: company lease has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Resource Management Act 1991
children.transBody: "법인 임차"란 「자원관리법 1991」 제2조제1항에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: conflict
children.body:
conflict means that—
(a) there is a difference that exceeds the applicable accuracy standards— (i) between the estate boundary and the boundary recorded in an approved CSD; or (ii) between the same boundary as recorded in different approved CSDs; or (iii) between the same boundary as recorded in an approved CSD and other evidence, including field evidence; and
(b) the difference has not been resolved by 1 or more approved CSDs
children.origBody:
conflict means that—
(a) there is a difference that exceeds the applicable accuracy standards— (i) between the estate boundary and the boundary recorded in an approved CSD; or (ii) between the same boundary as recorded in different approved CSDs; or (iii) between the same boundary as recorded in an approved CSD and other evidence, including field evidence; and
(b) the difference has not been resolved by 1 or more approved CSDs
children.transBody:
"충돌"이란 다음을 모두 갖춘 것을 말한다.
(a) 다음 사이에 해당 정확도 기준을 넘는 차이가 있을 것
 (i) 권리 경계와 승인된 성과묶음에 적힌 경계 사이
 (ii) 서로 다른 승인된 성과묶음에 적힌 같은 경계 사이
 (iii) 승인된 성과묶음에 적힌 경계와, 현지 증거를 포함한 다른 증거 사이
(b) 그 차이가 하나 이상의 승인된 성과묶음으로 풀리지 아니하였을 것

children.title: cross lease
children.body: cross lease has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Resource Management Act 1991
children.origBody: cross lease has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Resource Management Act 1991
children.transBody: "교차임차"란 「자원관리법 1991」 제2조제1항에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: CSD
children.body: CSD means cadastral survey dataset
children.origBody: CSD means cadastral survey dataset
children.transBody: "성과묶음(CSD)"이란 지적측량 성과묶음을 말한다.

children.title: CSD number
children.body: CSD number means the CSD type and identifier
children.origBody: CSD number means the CSD type and identifier
children.transBody: "성과묶음 번호"란 성과묶음의 종류와 식별자를 말한다.

children.title: deposited
children.body: deposited means deposited with the Registrar under the Land Transfer Act 2017
children.origBody: deposited means deposited with the Registrar under the Land Transfer Act 2017
children.transBody: "등록된"이란 「토지이전법 2017」에 따라 등기관에게 등록된 것을 말한다.

children.title: disturbed survey mark
children.body: disturbed survey mark means an old survey mark that is in a different position from where it was originally placed, but does not include a change of position due to Canterbury earthquake movement or fault zone movement
children.origBody: disturbed survey mark means an old survey mark that is in a different position from where it was originally placed, but does not include a change of position due to Canterbury earthquake movement or fault zone movement
children.transBody: "흔들린 측량표지"란 처음 설치한 자리와 다른 자리에 있는 옛 측량표지를 말한다. 다만, 캔터베리 지진 변동이나 단층대 변동으로 자리가 바뀐 것은 제외한다.

children.title: esplanade strip
children.body: esplanade strip has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Resource Management Act 1991
children.origBody: esplanade strip has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Resource Management Act 1991
children.transBody: "해안 산책 완충대"란 「자원관리법 1991」 제2조제1항에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: estate boundary
children.body:
estate boundary means the boundary of an estate recorded in a tenure system for—
(a) a fee simple estate; or
(b) Māori freehold land; or
(c) Māori customary land; or
(d) land of the Crown; or
(e) a stratum estate; or
(f) a leasehold estate
children.origBody:
estate boundary means the boundary of an estate recorded in a tenure system for—

children.transBody:

(a) 자유보유권(fee simple)

(c) 마오리 관습지
(d) 국유지
(e) 층별 구분권(stratum estate)
(f) 임차권

children.title: extinguished
children.body: extinguished , in relation to an existing parcel, means intended to no longer be available for the assignment of rights
children.origBody: extinguished , in relation to an existing parcel, means intended to no longer be available for the assignment of rights
children.transBody: "소멸된"이란 기존 필지에 대하여 더 이상 권리를 매길 수 없게 하려는 것을 말한다.

children.title: fault zone movement
children.body: fault zone movement has the meaning given to it by rule 108
children.origBody: fault zone movement has the meaning given to it by rule 108
children.transBody: "단층대 변동"이란 제108조에서 정하는 뜻을 말한다.

children.title: fixed marginal strip
children.body: fixed marginal strip means a marginal strip under section 24(3) of the Conservation Act 1987
children.origBody: fixed marginal strip means a marginal strip under section 24(3) of the Conservation Act 1987
children.transBody: "고정 연안 완충대"란 「자연보전법 1987」 제24조제3항에 따른 연안 완충대를 말한다.

children.title: Hawke’s Bay interim title
children.body: Hawke’s Bay interim title means a record of title issued under section 6 or 8 of the Land Transfer (Hawke’s Bay) Act 1931
children.origBody: Hawke’s Bay interim title means a record of title issued under section 6 or 8 of the Land Transfer (Hawke’s Bay) Act 1931
children.transBody: "호크스베이 임시 권리증"이란 「토지이전(호크스베이)법 1931」 제6조 또는 제8조에 따라 발급된 권리증을 말한다.

children.title: inaccurately determined
children.body: inaccurately determined means the relationship between the non-primary parcel boundary and the underlying parcel is not accurately defined
children.origBody: inaccurately determined means the relationship between the non-primary parcel boundary and the underlying parcel is not accurately defined
children.transBody: "부정확하게 정한"이란 부(副) 필지 경계와 기초 필지 사이의 관계를 정확하게 정하지 아니한 것을 말한다.

children.title: Māori customary land
children.body: Māori customary land has the same meaning as in section 4 of Te Ture Whenua Māori Act 1993
children.origBody: Māori customary land has the same meaning as in section 4 of Te Ture Whenua Māori Act 1993
children.transBody: "마오리 관습지"란 「테 투레 훼누아 마오리법 1993」 제4조에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: Māori freehold land
children.body: Māori freehold land has the same meaning as in section 4 of Te Ture Whenua Māori Act 1993
children.origBody: Māori freehold land has the same meaning as in section 4 of Te Ture Whenua Māori Act 1993
children.transBody: "마오리 자유보유지"란 「테 투레 훼누아 마오리법 1993」 제4조에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: marginal strip
children.body: marginal strip has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Conservation Act 1987
children.origBody: marginal strip has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Conservation Act 1987
children.transBody: "연안 완충대"란 「자연보전법 1987」 제2조제1항에서 정하는 뜻과 같다.

children.title: MHWS
children.body: MHWS means mean high-water springs
children.origBody: MHWS means mean high-water springs
children.transBody: "MHWS"란 대조평균고조면(큰사리 때의 평균 만조면)을 말한다.

children.title: MLWS
children.body: MLWS means mean low-water springs
children.origBody: MLWS means mean low-water springs
children.transBody: "MLWS"란 대조평균저조면(큰사리 때의 평균 간조면)을 말한다.

children.title: movable marginal strip
children.body: movable marginal strip means a marginal strip as defined in section 2(1) of the Conservation Act 1987, except a fixed marginal strip created under section 24(3) of that Act
children.origBody: movable marginal strip means a marginal strip as defined in section 2(1) of the Conservation Act 1987, except a fixed marginal strip created under section 24(3) of that Act
children.transBody: "가동 연안 완충대"란 「자연보전법 1987」 제2조제1항에서 정하는 연안 완충대를 말한다. 다만, 같은 법 제24조제3항에 따라 만들어진 고정 연안 완충대는 제외한다.

children.title: non-boundary mark
children.body: non-boundary mark means a survey mark that is not on a boundary point
children.origBody: non-boundary mark means a survey mark that is not on a boundary point
children.transBody: "비(非)경계표지"란 경계점 위에 있지 아니한 측량표지를 말한다.

children.title: non-primary parcel
children.body:
non-primary parcel —
(a) means any parcel that is not a primary parcel; and
(b) includes— (i) an easement, including an esplanade strip or an access strip: (ii) a covenant: (iii) a lease or an area associated with a lease: (iv) a licence or a permit area: (v) a unit or common property for the purposes of the Unit Titles Act 2010 : (vi) a movable marginal strip: (vii) a roadway or a restricted roadway that is an encumbrance over a primary parcel: (viii) a right over the common marine and coastal area
children.origBody:
non-primary parcel —
(a) means any parcel that is not a primary parcel; and
(b) includes— (i) an easement, including an esplanade strip or an access strip: (ii) a covenant: (iii) a lease or an area associated with a lease: (iv) a licence or a permit area: (v) a unit or common property for the purposes of the Unit Titles Act 2010 : (vi) a movable marginal strip: (vii) a roadway or a restricted roadway that is an encumbrance over a primary parcel: (viii) a right over the common marine and coastal area
children.transBody:
"부(副) 필지"란 다음을 말한다.
(a) 주 필지가 아닌 모든 필지를 말한다.
(b) 다음을 포함한다.
 (i) 지역권(해안 산책 완충대와 진입 통로대를 포함한다)
 (ii) 약정
 (iii) 임차 또는 임차에 딸린 구역
 (iv) 사용허가 또는 허가 구역
 (v) 「구분소유법 2010」에 따른 구분 단위 또는 공용부분
 (vi) 가동 연안 완충대
 (vii) 주 필지에 부담으로 얹힌 통행로 또는 제한 통행로
 (viii) 공유 해면·연안구역에 대한 권리

children.title: official projection
children.body: official projection means a projection, as defined in Schedule 3 , for use in a specific area
children.origBody: official projection means a projection, as defined in Schedule 3 , for use in a specific area
children.transBody: "공식 투영법"이란 별표 3에서 정하는, 특정 지역에 쓰는 투영법을 말한다.

children.title: old survey mark
children.body: old survey mark means a survey mark measured on the survey that is from the national survey control system or from an approved CSD
children.origBody: old survey mark means a survey mark measured on the survey that is from the national survey control system or from an approved CSD
children.transBody: "옛 측량표지"란 국가 측량기준점망이나 승인된 성과묶음에서 온 것으로서 그 측량에서 관측한 측량표지를 말한다.

children.title: parcel
children.body: parcel means an area or a space that is a single contiguous portion of land separately identified in a CSD or in the cadastre
children.origBody: parcel means an area or a space that is a single contiguous portion of land separately identified in a CSD or in the cadastre
children.transBody: "필지"란 성과묶음이나 지적에 따로 표시된, 서로 이어진 하나의 토지 구역 또는 공간을 말한다.

children.title: parcel intent
children.body: parcel intent means a description of a right or an interest intended to be assigned to a parcel
children.origBody: parcel intent means a description of a right or an interest intended to be assigned to a parcel
children.transBody: "필지의 용도 구분"이란 그 필지에 매기려는 권리나 이익에 대한 표시를 말한다.

children.title: permanent reference mark
children.body: permanent reference mark or PRM means a reference mark that complies with rule 33
children.origBody: permanent reference mark or PRM means a reference mark that complies with rule 33
children.transBody: "영구 참조표지(PRM)"란 제33조에 맞는 참조표지를 말한다.

children.title: PRM
children.body: permanent reference mark or PRM means a reference mark that complies with rule 33
children.origBody: permanent reference mark or PRM means a reference mark that complies with rule 33
children.transBody: "영구 참조표지(PRM)"란 제33조에 맞는 참조표지를 말한다.

children.title: permanent structure boundary
children.body:
permanent structure boundary means—
(a) a boundary related to a building or recognisable physical structure that is likely to remain undisturbed for 50 years or more; or
(b) the outline of a future development unit
children.origBody:
permanent structure boundary means—

(b) the outline of a future development unit
children.transBody:
"영구 구조물 경계"란 다음을 말한다.
(a) 앞으로 50년 이상 흔들림 없이 남아 있을 것으로 보이는 건물이나 알아볼 수 있는 물리적 구조물에 딸린 경계
(b) 장래 개발용 구획의 외곽선

children.title: primary parcel
children.body:
primary parcel means any parcel that is intended to be—
(a) owned by the Crown, except a movable marginal strip parcel; or
(b) held in fee simple; or
(c) Māori freehold land or Māori customary land; or
(d) part of the common marine and coastal area; or
(e) the bed of a lake or river; or
(f) a road or railway parcel; or
(g) vested in a local authority

children.title: residue parcel
children.body:
residue parcel means the residual portion of a primary parcel—
(a) that remains as a result of a survey— (i) for removal of limitations as to parcels; or (ii) for an adverse possession claim; or (iii) to change the registration of land from the Deeds Registration Act 1908 to the Land Transfer Act 2017 ; or
(b) that— (i) is being defined as part of the bed of a lake or a river, or part of the common marine and coastal area; and (ii) is not currently recorded in the cadastre as the bed of a lake or a river, or part of the common marine and coastal area; and (iii) is not intended to vest; and (iv) is not intended to have a new estate record

tree.transBody:
공식 측지기준계는 뉴질랜드 측지기준계 2000(NZGD2000)으로 한다. 이 기준계는 LINZS25000 「뉴질랜드 측지기준계 2000 표준」에서 정한다.
공식 투영법은 다음의 NZGD2000 횡메르카토르 2000 자오선권 투영법으로 한다.
[뉴질랜드 본섬] Mount Eden 2000 · Bay of Plenty 2000 · Poverty Bay 2000 · Hawkes Bay 2000 · Taranaki 2000 · Tuhirangi 2000 · Wanganui 2000 · Wairarapa 2000 · Wellington 2000 · Collingwood 2000 · Nelson 2000 · Karamea 2000 · Buller 2000 · Grey 2000 · Amuri 2000 · Marlborough 2000 · Hokitika 2000 · Okarito 2000 · Jacksons Bay 2000 · Mount Pleasant 2000 · Gawler 2000 · Timaru 2000 · Lindis Peak 2000 · Mount Nicholas 2000 · Mount York 2000 · Observation Point 2000 · North Taieri 2000 · Bluff 2000

위 투영법은 LINZS25002 「뉴질랜드 측지기준계 2000 투영법 표준」에서 정한다.

tree.title: Cadastral survey network marks
tree.body:
A survey mark is suitable for use as a cadastral survey network mark if it has been assigned a NZGD2000 coordinate with a Landonline order 6 or better.
Landonline orders are defined in LINZS25006: Standard for tiers, classes, and orders of LINZ data.
tree.transBody:
측량표지는 Landonline 등급 6 이상의 NZGD2000 좌표가 부여된 경우 지적측량 기준점망 표지로 쓸 수 있다.
Landonline 등급은 LINZS25006 「LINZ 자료의 계층·등급·차수 표준」에서 정한다.

children.title: NZVD2016
children.body: The official vertical datum is New Zealand Vertical Datum 2016 ( NZVD2016 ).

children.transBody: 공식 수직기준은 뉴질랜드 수직기준 2016(NZVD2016)으로 한다.

tree.title: Vertical control marks
tree.body:
A survey mark is suitable for the vertical control of cadastral surveys if it has been assigned a height in terms of an official vertical datum with a Landonline order 3V or better.
Landonline orders are defined in LINZS25006: Standard for tiers, classes, and orders of LINZ data.
tree.transBody:
측량표지는 공식 수직기준에 따른 표고가 Landonline 등급 3V 이상으로 부여된 경우 지적측량의 수직 기준점으로 쓸 수 있다.
Landonline 등급은 LINZS25006 「LINZ 자료의 계층·등급·차수 표준」에서 정한다.
